# 白井光太郎『植物渡来考』— THE AUTHORITY ON WHEN PLANTS REACHED JAPAN
# NDL pid 1189709 (1929 ed.); also pids 1903747 (1931), 1855758-adjacent, 1382031 (1967).
# Quoted from the NDL full-text index, 2026-08-31. NO SCAN IS HELD.

アカナス
漢名 蕃柿 一名六月柿 一名小金瓜
和名 サンゴジユナスビ
來歷 南亞米利加の原產なり。支那にては群芳譜に始めて記載す。
日本の書にては後藤梨春の物品目錄に載す。

"AKANASU. Chinese names: fanshi, also liuyue-shi, also xiaojingua. Japanese
name: sangoju-nasubi. ORIGIN: native to South America. In China it is first
recorded in the QUNFANG PU. In Japanese books it is recorded in GOTŌ RISHUN'S
BUPPIN MOKUROKU."

This is the sentence that identifies the earliest Japanese record. It also
independently confirms the Qunfang Pu as the first Chinese record, which this
project has verified from three facsimiles (1708, 1725, 1728).
